prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one polished 16:9 landscape visual concept for the PLAYABLE PREPARATION SCREEN of the French cozy fantasy browser game "Le monde tient dans une valise". Design for actual 960 x 540 display, with very legible uncluttered objects and generous interaction space. This is a single game-screen composition, not a collage, not a presentation board, no device frame.
Art direction: hand-painted 2D storybook game illustration, gently rounded forms, confident warm brown contours, rich restrained colors, soft painterly volumes; match a cream travel notebook, caramel leather, aged brass, turquoise and lavender magic. Crisp smooth edges, not pixel art, not photorealistic, not shiny generic mobile-game UI. Calm desaturated deep teal tabletop background, warm soft light; no scenic landscape or distracting props.

Layout: a LARGE FRONT-FACING PERFECTLY ROUND MAGIC COMPASS occupies the left 42% of screen, and a BEAUTIFUL OPEN LEATHER SUITCASE in stylized three-quarter isometric perspective occupies right 53%. Both fully visible with margins. Compact heading above them "Préparons le voyage". Small secondary navigation bottom left "Accueil". Main departure button bottom right "Voyager" on a torn warm parchment tag with two subtle pieces of translucent tape, not a green button. Do not add inventory bars, sticker collections, settings icons, decorative extra objects or extra buttons.

Compass: broad aged brass rim, cream parchment dial with subtle engraved eight-point compass rose. NO winding crowns, NO watch lugs, NO watch chain, NO top ring, NO clock numbers, NO clock hands. Exactly TEN small hand-painted elemental icons evenly spaced around its rim, clockwise starting from top: 1 round leafy TREE, 2 purple MUSHROOM, 3 turquoise WATER wave, 4 coral FIRE flame, 5 blue-gray ROCK, 6 PALM tree, 7 icy SNOWflake, 8 pale lavender CLOUD, 9 sandstone ruined ARCH, 10 violet-cyan CRYSTAL cluster. All ten clearly different. Ten icons only, no invented elements.
Exactly TWO independent sharp ornate compass needles sharing one brass pivot. The turquoise first needle is a long pointed openwork spear with a small diamond counterweight; it points toward WATER in the upper right of the dial. The violet second needle is a narrower pointed arrow with a small brass-rimmed circular magnifying lens as its counterweight; it points down toward PALM at the bottom of the dial. Needle shapes look like real magical navigation instruments, robust and tactile, not stubby clock hands. They stop before covering the elemental icons. They are two distinct needles, not two ends of a single needle.
Under compass two discreet readable cream selection labels: "1 · Eau" and "2 · Palmier". Nearby smaller separate readable energy text "Charges : 10 / 10".

Suitcase: caramel brown leather, deep warm brown seams, rounded reinforced brass corners and clasps, substantial leather handle on the front. Open lid behind, empty moss-teal fabric lining inside the lid, simple crossed leather retaining straps. Inside the BOTTOM tray exactly TWO side-by-side fitted shallow oval padded compartments in warm cream fabric, separated by a slim leather divider. They contain two lovely dimensional painted miniature figurines: one small turquoise wave on the left, one curved little palm tree on a sand-colored base on the right. These are objects inside a suitcase, not worlds, dioramas or landscape portals. Strong easy-to-read silhouettes matching the same WATER and PALM icons on compass. Nothing else in the suitcase, no stickers.
Composition priority: it must immediately read as turning two compass needles to choose two miniatures in a travel suitcase. Keep all text sparse, French spelled correctly, large readable. No glow storm, particles, glitter, extra mechanics, logos, watermark. Render a confident beautiful coherent game art proposal with room for real controls.
